message.content:
The 19th‑century sculpture that is most often cited as the era’s iconic masterpiece is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin (1889)**. ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading French sculptor who bridged Romanticism and modernism | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Material** | Bronze (originally marble) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist – dynamic, textured surfaces that capture movement and emotion | | **Iconic Elements** | The intimate embrace, the subtle play of light on flesh, the almost unfinished surface that invites viewers to imagine the rest | | **Cultural Impact** | • Widely reproduced in prints, postcards, and museum displays worldwide.
• Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Influenced countless artists and remains a staple in art education. | ### Other contenders - **“The Gates of Hell” (1880‑1908)** – a monumental bronze relief series that showcases Rodin’s mastery of complex composition. - **“The Statue of Liberty” (1886)** – a monumental neoclassical sculpture that has become a global icon of freedom. - **“The Thinker” (1902)** – technically early 20th, but often grouped with Rodin’s 19th‑century oeuvre. ### Bottom line While many 19th‑century sculptures are celebrated, Rodin’s **“The Kiss”** is the most universally recognized and frequently referenced as the quintessential sculpture of that century.
